CYP2D6.desc: Hepatic enzyme metabolising ~25% of commonly prescribed drugs including opioids, antidepressants, tamoxifen and atomoxetine.

landing_notes.poor: Codeine/tramadol contraindicated (inefficacy). Dose reduction required for TCAs, SSRIs, tamoxifen and atomoxetine.
landing_notes.ultrarapid: Codeine/tramadol contraindicated (rapid morphine conversion — life-threatening toxicity). Antidepressant efficacy likely reduced.
landing_notes.intermediate: Reduced CYP2D6 activity. Consider dose adjustment for codeine, tramadol, TCAs and SSRIs; monitor closely.

drugs.name: Codeine / Tramadol
drugs.rec: PM: contraindicated (inefficacy / toxicity risk). UM: contraindicated (ultra-rapid morphine conversion). IM: use with caution; consider alternative.

drugs.name: Antidepressants (TCAs / SSRIs / SNRIs)
drugs.rec: PM: reduce TCA dose or select CYP2D6-independent agent. UM: standard doses may be sub-therapeutic; consider alternative.

drugs.name: Tamoxifen
drugs.rec: PM: tamoxifen may be ineffective — consider aromatase inhibitor where appropriate.

drugs.name: Atomoxetine
drugs.rec: PM: initiate at 50% standard dose; titrate slowly. UM: standard dose may be sub-therapeutic.

drugs.name: Aripiprazole
drugs.rec: CPIC rates this gene-drug pair Level B but has not published a guideline for it. For genotype-guided recommendations see the DPWG guideline annotation PA166104937 (ClinPGx).

CYP2C19.desc: Activates clopidogrel (prodrug); metabolises PPIs, antidepressants and voriconazole. Both loss-of-function (PM) and gain-of-function (UM/RM) phenotypes have distinct clinical consequences.

landing_notes.poor: Clopidogrel contraindicated — inadequate antiplatelet activation. Use prasugrel or ticagrelor. PPIs and SSRIs may accumulate.
landing_notes.ultrarapid: Voriconazole likely sub-therapeutic. PPI efficacy reduced. Monitor antidepressant levels.
landing_notes.rapid: Increased CYP2C19 activity. Consider voriconazole dose increase. Monitor PPI efficacy.
landing_notes.intermediate: Mildly reduced CYP2C19 activity. Monitor clopidogrel response; consider alternative antiplatelet.

drugs.name: Clopidogrel
drugs.rec: PM/IM: use alternative antiplatelet (prasugrel or ticagrelor). UM/RM: standard dose; enhanced response expected.

drugs.name: Antidepressants (SSRIs / TCAs)
drugs.rec: PM: reduce dose or select alternative. UM: standard or higher dose; monitor for sub-therapeutic levels.

drugs.name: Voriconazole
drugs.rec: PM: reduce dose substantially (elevated exposure, toxicity risk). UM/RM: TDM required; standard doses may be sub-therapeutic.

drugs.name: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs)
drugs.rec: PM: consider dose reduction (increased AUC). UM: may require higher dose for adequate acid suppression.

CYP2C9.desc: Metabolises the S-enantiomer of warfarin, NSAIDs and phenytoin. Poor metabolisers require significantly reduced doses of narrow-therapeutic-index drugs.

landing_notes.poor: Warfarin sensitivity: significantly reduced starting dose required. NSAID and phenytoin toxicity risk elevated.
landing_notes.intermediate: Moderate warfarin sensitivity. Consider dose reduction for NSAIDs and phenytoin; TDM recommended.

drugs.name: Warfarin
drugs.rec: PM: initiate at ≤25% of standard dose and titrate to INR. IM: reduce starting dose; use CPIC dosing calculator.

drugs.name: NSAIDs
drugs.rec: PM: use lowest effective dose or select alternative. Increased GI and renal toxicity risk.

drugs.name: Phenytoin / Fosphenytoin
drugs.rec: PM/IM: reduce maintenance dose by 25–50%; TDM essential to avoid toxicity.

DPYD.desc: Rate-limiting enzyme in 5-FU and capecitabine catabolism. Even heterozygous loss-of-function variants confer significant toxicity risk — CPIC recommends pre-emptive genotyping. WGS detects the full variant spectrum including reduced-function alleles *5 (c.1627A>G) and *9A (c.85T>C) that are not covered by standard pharmacogenomics arrays.

landing_notes.poor: Fluoropyrimidines (5-FU/capecitabine) are contraindicated — life-threatening toxicity risk.
landing_notes.intermediate: Fluoropyrimidine dose reduction (≥50%) required before initiating therapy. Consult CPIC/DPWG guidelines.
landing_notes.decreased: Reduced DPYD function. Fluoropyrimidine dose adjustment or avoidance required.
landing_notes._diplotype: Non-reference DPYD variant detected. Fluoropyrimidine (5-FU/capecitabine) dose adjustment or avoidance may be required — consult CPIC guidelines before prescribing.

drugs.name: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) / Capecitabine
drugs.rec: PM: contraindicated. IM/Decreased function: ≥50% dose reduction with therapeutic drug monitoring. Normal: standard dosing.

TPMT.desc: Inactivates thiopurines (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, thioguanine). Deficient patients accumulate toxic thioguanine nucleotides causing severe, potentially fatal myelosuppression.

landing_notes.poor: Thiopurines contraindicated at standard doses — life-threatening myelosuppression. Use alternative or dramatically reduce dose with TDM.
landing_notes.intermediate: Reduce thiopurine starting dose by 30–70% and titrate based on toxicity and response.

drugs.name: Azathioprine / 6-Mercaptopurine / Thioguanine
drugs.rec: PM: avoid or use ≤10% of standard dose with TDM. IM: reduce starting dose 30–70%; monitor CBC.

NUDT15.desc: Hydrolyses thioguanine nucleotide metabolites. Loss-of-function variants cause severe thiopurine-induced myelosuppression; particularly common in East Asian and Hispanic populations.

landing_notes.poor: Thiopurines contraindicated at standard doses — severe myelosuppression risk. Consider non-thiopurine immunosuppressant.
landing_notes.intermediate: Reduce thiopurine starting dose; monitor CBC closely for myelosuppression.

drugs.name: Azathioprine / 6-Mercaptopurine / Thioguanine
drugs.rec: PM: avoid or markedly reduce dose with TDM. IM: reduce starting dose; CBC monitoring mandatory.

SLCO1B1.desc: Hepatic uptake transporter (OATP1B1) for statins. Decreased function variants reduce hepatic statin clearance, increasing plasma exposure and myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk.

landing_notes.poor: High statin-associated myopathy risk. Use ≤20 mg/day simvastatin or switch to rosuvastatin/pravastatin.
landing_notes.decreased: Increased statin myopathy risk. Avoid high-dose simvastatin; consider lower-risk statin.
landing_notes.intermediate: Moderately increased statin exposure. Prefer rosuvastatin or pravastatin over simvastatin.

drugs.name: Simvastatin / Statins
drugs.rec: Poor/Decreased function: avoid simvastatin >20 mg/day; use rosuvastatin or pravastatin. IM: simvastatin ≤40 mg/day.

UGT1A1.desc: Glucuronidates irinotecan's active metabolite (SN-38) and bilirubin. Reduced activity (*28/*28, Gilbert's syndrome) substantially increases irinotecan toxicity risk. Note: promoter alleles *60 (rs45530432) and *80 (rs887829) compound the phenotype of *28 but are not uniformly represented across tool allele databases — individual tool outputs may differ.

landing_notes.poor: High irinotecan toxicity risk (*28/*28 — Gilbert's). Reduce irinotecan starting dose by at least one dose level.
landing_notes.intermediate: Mildly elevated irinotecan exposure. Standard starting dose with close toxicity monitoring.
landing_notes.decreased: Reduced UGT1A1 function — monitor for irinotecan and atazanavir toxicity.

drugs.name: Irinotecan
drugs.rec: PM (*28/*28): reduce starting dose by ≥1 dose level; titrate by toxicity. IM: standard dose with close monitoring.

drugs.name: Atazanavir
drugs.rec: PM: increased unconjugated bilirubin and jaundice risk — consider alternative antiretroviral.

CYP2B6.desc: Primary metaboliser of efavirenz and several other antiretrovirals. Poor metabolisers have ~4–5-fold elevated efavirenz plasma concentrations causing CNS toxicity.

landing_notes.poor: Efavirenz plasma levels ~4–5X elevated. Reduce efavirenz to 400 mg/day or switch to alternative ART regimen.
landing_notes.intermediate: Moderately elevated efavirenz exposure. Monitor for CNS side effects; consider dose adjustment.

drugs.name: Efavirenz
drugs.rec: PM: reduce dose to 400 mg/day or switch to alternative ART. IM: standard dose with CNS toxicity monitoring.

CYP3A5.desc: Major metaboliser of tacrolimus and other calcineurin inhibitors. Expressers (*1 carriers) require higher tacrolimus doses; non-expressers (*3/*3) achieve target levels at lower doses.

landing_notes.poor: CYP3A5 non-expresser (*3/*3): tacrolimus dose requirements typical for non-expressers. Use standard weight-based dosing with TDM.
landing_notes.intermediate: Intermediate CYP3A5 expression. TDM-guided tacrolimus dosing essential.

drugs.name: Tacrolimus
drugs.rec: Non-expresser (*3/*3): standard dose + TDM. Expresser (*1 carrier): initiate at 1.5–2X standard dose to achieve target trough.

VKORC1.desc: Warfarin target enzyme. rs9923231 (−1639G>A) in the VKORC1 promoter reduces enzyme expression, substantially increasing warfarin sensitivity and bleeding risk.

landing_notes._diplotype: VKORC1 rs9923231 detected — increased warfarin sensitivity. Initiate warfarin at a reduced dose. A/A homozygotes require the greatest reduction (~3 mg/day). Use CPIC warfarin dosing calculator.

drugs.name: Warfarin
drugs.rec: A/A homozygote: initiate at ~3 mg/day and titrate to INR. A/G heterozygote: intermediate sensitivity; reduce starting dose. Use CPIC calculator incorporating CYP2C9 + VKORC1 + CYP4F2.

G6PD.desc: X-linked enzyme protecting erythrocytes from oxidative damage. Deficiency causes acute drug-induced haemolytic anaemia with rasburicase, primaquine and other oxidant agents.

landing_notes.deficient: G6PD deficiency: rasburicase is contraindicated (severe haemolytic anaemia risk). Avoid primaquine, dapsone and high-dose aspirin.
landing_notes.variable: Partial G6PD activity. Avoid high-risk oxidant drugs; rasburicase requires careful risk-benefit assessment.
landing_notes.intermediate: Intermediate G6PD activity. Monitor for haemolytic events with oxidant drug exposure.

drugs.name: Rasburicase
drugs.rec: Deficient: contraindicated — risk of severe, potentially fatal haemolytic anaemia. Variable: use with extreme caution, monitoring haemoglobin.

NAT2.desc: N-acetyltransferase 2 is a phase II acetylating enzyme that metabolises hydralazine. CPIC rates hydralazine Level A: dose to NAT2 phenotype (poor metabolizers need a lower starting dose and carry a higher risk of drug-induced lupus; rapid and intermediate metabolizers need a higher dose). Isoniazid is CPIC Level C and is not flagged.

landing_notes.poor: NAT2 poor metabolizer (slow acetylator): hydralazine exposure is increased, with higher efficacy and adverse-effect risk including drug-induced lupus. CPIC: start at a total daily dose of 40-75 mg and titrate carefully.
landing_notes.slow: NAT2 poor metabolizer (slow acetylator): hydralazine exposure is increased, with higher efficacy and adverse-effect risk including drug-induced lupus. CPIC: start at a total daily dose of 40-75 mg and titrate carefully.
landing_notes.intermediate: NAT2 intermediate metabolizer: reduced hydralazine exposure and efficacy compared with poor metabolizers. CPIC: consider a starting total daily dose of at least 75 mg and titrate up to 300 mg as tolerated.
landing_notes.rapid: NAT2 rapid metabolizer: reduced hydralazine exposure and efficacy compared with poor metabolizers. CPIC: consider a starting total daily dose of at least 75 mg and titrate up to 300 mg as tolerated.

drugs.name: Hydralazine
drugs.rec: PM: start at a total daily dose of 40-75 mg and titrate carefully to clinical effect; use caution at 200 mg/day or more (higher exposure, drug-induced lupus risk). IM and RM: consider a starting total daily dose of at least 75 mg and titrate up to 300 mg/day as tolerated; they typically need a 50-100% higher maintenance dose than PMs.

RYR1.desc: Skeletal muscle calcium release channel. Pathogenic variants confer susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia (MH) — a life-threatening reaction to volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine.

landing_notes._diplotype: Non-reference RYR1 variant detected. Evaluate for malignant hyperthermia susceptibility — avoid volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine if susceptible.
landing_notes.susceptible: Malignant hyperthermia susceptibility: avoid all volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine. Use TIVA. Ensure dantrolene is immediately available.

drugs.name: Volatile anaesthetic agents
drugs.rec: MH-susceptible: contraindicated. Use total intravenous anaesthesia (TIVA) only; dantrolene must be immediately available.

drugs.name: Succinylcholine
drugs.rec: MH-susceptible: contraindicated. Use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers (e.g. rocuronium with sugammadex reversal).

CACNA1S.desc: Skeletal muscle L-type calcium channel subunit. Pathogenic variants (e.g. *2 Arg174Trp, *3 Arg1086His) confer malignant hyperthermia susceptibility (MHS) — a life-threatening pharmacogenomic reaction to volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine. Partner gene to RYR1 under the same CPIC guideline.

landing_notes._diplotype: Non-reference CACNA1S variant detected. Evaluate for malignant hyperthermia susceptibility — avoid volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine if susceptible.
landing_notes.susceptible: Malignant hyperthermia susceptibility: avoid all volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine. Use TIVA. Ensure dantrolene is immediately available.
landing_notes.mhs: Malignant hyperthermia susceptibility: avoid all volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine. Use TIVA. Ensure dantrolene is immediately available.

drugs.name: Volatile anaesthetic agents
drugs.rec: MH-susceptible: contraindicated. Use total intravenous anaesthesia (TIVA) only; dantrolene must be immediately available.

drugs.name: Succinylcholine
drugs.rec: MH-susceptible: contraindicated. Use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers (e.g. rocuronium with sugammadex reversal).

MT-RNR1.desc: Mitochondrial 12S ribosomal RNA gene. Variants m.1555A>G (~1/500 Europeans) and m.1494C>T confer ribosomal hypersensitivity to aminoglycosides — even a single standard dose can cause permanent bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Maternally inherited; affects all maternal-lineage family members.

landing_notes._diplotype: CPIC Level A MT-RNR1 variant detected. Avoid aminoglycosides unless no safe alternatives exist.
landing_notes.aminoglycoside-ototoxicity risk: Aminoglycoside-ototoxicity risk: avoid gentamicin, tobramycin, amikacin, streptomycin and neomycin unless essential. Counsel patient on irreversible hearing-loss risk. Inform maternal-lineage family members.

drugs.name: Aminoglycosides (gentamicin, tobramycin, amikacin, streptomycin, neomycin)
drugs.rec: m.1555A>G or m.1494C>T carrier: avoid aminoglycosides if alternatives exist. If unavoidable, use lowest effective dose with audiological monitoring. Inform maternal relatives.

CYP4F2.desc: Metabolises vitamin K1; V433M (*3 allele) reduces vitamin K catabolism, modestly increasing warfarin sensitivity. Incorporated in CPIC warfarin dosing algorithm.

landing_notes._diplotype: CYP4F2 *3 variant detected — minor contribution to warfarin sensitivity. Use CPIC warfarin dosing calculator incorporating CYP2C9 + VKORC1 + CYP4F2 genotype.

drugs.name: Warfarin
drugs.rec: *3 carriers may require slightly higher warfarin doses. Incorporate into multi-gene CPIC dosing algorithm alongside CYP2C9 and VKORC1.

ABCG2.desc: Efflux transporter (BCRP) reducing intestinal and hepatic uptake of rosuvastatin and other statins. The *2 variant (rs2231142, c.421C>A, p.Gln141Lys) decreases transporter function, increasing statin plasma exposure.

landing_notes._diplotype: ABCG2 rs2231142 (c.421C>A) detected — decreased rosuvastatin transport. Consider lower rosuvastatin starting dose (≤10 mg/day) per CPIC guidelines.
landing_notes.decreased: ABCG2 decreased function — reduced rosuvastatin efflux increases plasma exposure. Use lower starting dose.

drugs.name: Rosuvastatin
drugs.rec: ABCG2 decreased function (*2/*2 or *2/ref): initiate rosuvastatin at ≤10 mg/day. Consider alternative statin if high-intensity therapy required.

HLA-A.desc: Major histocompatibility complex class I gene. HLA-A*31:01 is associated with carbamazepine-induced severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCAR) including DRESS, SJS, and TEN across all ancestries.

risk_alleles.A*31:01: carbamazepine: increased DRESS/SJS/TEN risk across all ancestries

HLA-A.no_risk_note: No CPIC Level A high-risk HLA-A alleles (A*31:01) detected.

landing_notes._diplotype: HLA-A*31:01 detected — carbamazepine associated with severe cutaneous adverse reactions (DRESS, SJS, TEN) across all ancestries. Avoid if clinically feasible.

drugs.name: Carbamazepine
drugs.rec: HLA-A*31:01 positive: avoid carbamazepine — significantly increased risk of DRESS, SJS, TEN in all ancestries. Use alternative anticonvulsant.

HLA-B.desc: Major histocompatibility complex class I gene. Multiple HLA-B alleles are associated with severe drug hypersensitivity: HLA-B*57:01 (abacavir), HLA-B*58:01 (allopurinol), HLA-B*15:02 (carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine/phenytoin in Asian ancestry).

risk_alleles.B*15:02: carbamazepine / oxcarbazepine / phenytoin: avoid — high SJS/TEN risk (esp. Asian ancestry)

HLA-B.no_risk_note: No high-risk HLA-B alleles (B*57:01, B*15:02, B*58:01 [CPIC Level A]) detected.

landing_notes._diplotype: High-risk HLA-B allele detected — see detail page for drug-specific recommendations.

drugs.name: Abacavir
drugs.rec: HLA-B*57:01 positive: abacavir contraindicated — high risk of severe, potentially life-threatening hypersensitivity reaction. Use alternative ART regimen.

drugs.name: Allopurinol
drugs.rec: HLA-B*58:01 positive: avoid allopurinol — high risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis. Use alternative urate-lowering therapy.

drugs.name: Carbamazepine
drugs.rec: HLA-B*15:02 positive: avoid carbamazepine — high SJS/TEN risk especially in Han Chinese and Southeast Asian ancestry. Use alternative anticonvulsant.

drugs.name: Oxcarbazepine
drugs.rec: HLA-B*15:02 positive: avoid oxcarbazepine — high SJS/TEN risk especially in Han Chinese and Southeast Asian ancestry. Use alternative anticonvulsant.

drugs.name: Phenytoin / Fosphenytoin
drugs.rec: HLA-B*15:02 positive: increased SJS risk. Avoid or use with extreme caution; consider alternative anticonvulsant.

CYP1A1.desc: CYP1A1 metabolises polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and some drugs. No CPIC Level A/B guideline exists; informational star-allele calling only.

CYP1A2.desc: CYP1A2 is a major hepatic CYP enzyme (~13% of total hepatic CYP activity). CPIC has no CYP1A2 gene-drug pair, so the gene is typed but no pair is listed or flagged.

CYP2A6.desc: CYP2A6 is the principal enzyme catalysing nicotine C-oxidation to cotinine. CPIC has no CYP2A6 gene-drug pair, so the gene is typed but no pair is listed or flagged.

CYP2C8.desc: CYP2C8 metabolises pioglitazone, paclitaxel and other drugs. CPIC rates its pairs Level C, so the gene is typed but no pair is listed or flagged.

CYP2E1.desc: CYP2E1 metabolises ethanol, paracetamol (acetaminophen), and industrial solvents. No CPIC guideline with actionable recommendations currently exists.

CYP3A4.desc: CYP3A4 is the most abundant hepatic CYP enzyme, metabolising ~50% of drugs. The *22 allele (rs35599367) reduces CYP3A4 expression. CPIC rates CYP3A4 pairs Level C, so the gene is typed but no gene-drug pair is listed or flagged.

GSTM1.desc: GSTM1 (glutathione S-transferase mu 1) is commonly deleted (*0/*0 null genotype), reducing glutathione conjugation capacity. The null genotype is present in ~50% of Europeans and ~35% of Asians. No CPIC Level A/B guideline with dose-adjustment recommendations currently exists.

GSTT1.desc: GSTT1 (glutathione S-transferase theta 1) null genotype (*0/*0) is present in ~15–20% of Europeans. No CPIC Level A/B guideline with dose-adjustment recommendations currently exists.

IFNL3.desc: IFNL3 (IL28B) encodes interferon lambda-3 (rs12979860). The peginterferon pairs are Retired in CPIC, so the gene is typed but no gene-drug pair is listed or flagged.

NAT1.desc: NAT1 (N-acetyltransferase 1) acetyltransferase with activity toward aromatic and heterocyclic amines. No CPIC Level A/B guideline with actionable dose recommendations currently exists.

POR.desc: POR (cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase) is the essential electron donor for all microsomal CYP enzymes. POR *28 (A503V) is the most common variant and modestly alters the activity of multiple CYPs. No standalone CPIC guideline exists; interpret POR variants in context of co-metabolising CYP genotypes.
